P1.evidence: Setter contact acknowledged but not read back in detail — 'I heard you and Kyla had a good conversation the other day. I got some of the details about that. But yeah, we might ask you a few of the same questions just to make sure we don't miss anything.' Better than a cold open, short of making him feel seen. The frame ran three of four parts: 'Just want to understand more about you, what's going on with your fitness, what are you looking to accomplish, and then we have alignment there. can go into all the details about what we do' — where he is, where he wants to go, and what happens next, but nothing on what is in the way or what he needs. Frame agreement was explicitly sought and given: 'if that sounds good' → 'A hundred percent.' The open question ran in its strongest form: 'curious in your opinion to hear what, what do you think is the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?'

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch. Weight asked directly — 'What are you weighing in now?' → 236 — and historical fighting weight established at 205 with 'How long has it been since you were, let's call it fighting weight?'. Age was volunteered, height never obtained. Occupation established but never the desk-versus-on-feet question. Health conditions asked directly: 'Any like chronic conditions with your health or anything?' Injuries were the standout — 'What did you injure?' produced the full back-injury history, and 'Do you have any current, like you said, it's not really affecting you now. Do you have any aches or pains or any old injuries that come up?' followed up properly. Training week fully mapped: 'are you doing any exercises right now?' then 'when did you start doing that routine?' produced an honest day-by-day account ending in 'if I have to be honest, I'll probably do like two and a half days of solid, solid workout'. Results asked: 'have you been seeing improvements from doing that? Like, have you been dropping the weight?' Diet asked: 'How's your eating?' which surfaced the IBS. Energy asked: 'how your energy levels'. Sleep was never asked — the prospect volunteered the new bed, the magnesium and the caffeine taper off the back of the energy question.

P3.evidence: By some distance the best goals work in this batch. Body areas asked directly: 'what were some of the areas of your body that you were talking about?' → legs, flexibility, high kicks, windmills. The can't-do-physically question ran hard via 'is there any particular reason you don't just go back to that and kind of get the camaraderie and the flexibility out of just doing what you used to do?', which produced the CTE fear, the cracked rib and the jiu-jitsu ambition. The bridge ran twice — 'what was it that caused that realization for you a few weeks ago?' and later 'Was that like always your mindset or did that change?' The who-else question ran explicitly and is the single best moment of the batch: 'You mentioned something interesting with the competing in jujitsu about, like, inspiring your kids. And why is that important for you?' — which produced 'they made a comment that really hurt me, but in a good way, which is, oh, dad's always been like that. He's always been trying to lose weight, but he doesn't.' What is missing is the reflect-back. The rep had 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about your kids not remembering you strong' sitting right there and instead summarised the training situation. That reframe, delivered at that moment, is what would have made the payment logistics feel urgent an hour later.

P4.evidence: Past attempts fully surfaced — MMA, running, Onnit kettlebell programmes, the gym with his buddy, the ChatGPT-selected thruster routine — via 'when did you start doing the kettlebells', 'why Trevor?' and 'is there any particular reason you don't just go back to that'. What happened with them was asked and answered honestly. The prospect named the gap himself, unprompted and precisely: no routine, no excitement, no accountability, no camaraderie. The rep then delivered a genuine root-cause observation that deserves credit: 'it seems like for you, it's like there's always, like, an external motivator, which is fine, but at one point it was MMA, and then the Air Force' — that is real diagnostic work. But he stopped one step short. He never converted it into the structural point the phase exists for, and never asked the scripted 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?', which this prospect had already half-answered and would have answered fully.

P5.evidence: The phase never ran, and this is the clearest example in the batch of the difference between the prospect supplying material and the rep earning it. Jay delivered his own consequence frame unprompted — 'I'm surrounded by people who I can draw inspiration from, right, who are in their 50s and stuff, and they can't even turn around and wipe their [ass]. So it's like, do you want to be like that? No.' and 'It's my one time on this earth, and this is the one body I get. I don't have a reset button.' The rep never asked the two-year question, never asked whether he was willing to settle, never asked why not. The nearest scripted move was the readiness question — 'you feel like you're ready to start making changes and actually sticking to a program and going for it?' → 'I don't have a choice, bro' — which counts as a partial line in the sand. Because the phase was never run by the rep, there was no owned cost of inaction to return to when the payment stalled.

P6.evidence: A clear yes was obtained before the price, which is the right order and the only call in this batch where that happened: 'maybe on a scale one to 10, one being sounds like [crap], 10 is like, dude, this is exactly what I'm looking for' → 'Oh, no, definitely, definitely a 10, bro.' That satisfies P6c. But it measures enthusiasm for the offer, not belief that he can get there with the right structure, and the second question never ran at all. 'If you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' is precisely the question that would have surfaced the bank-account problem before the price rather than fifteen minutes after it, when there was still time in the call to solve it.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and every step failed. No payment collected. No payment link sent — the rep handed the action to the prospect: 'just shoot me a text. I'll shoot you over the link.' No onboarding call with Trevor booked; the timing was worked out conversationally to 'it would be Monday' and never placed on a calendar. The agreement was described as a future step rather than signed on the call. The Skool link, welcome email and questionnaire were never mentioned. Partial credit is due for offering a deposit — 'Other options we can do a deposit now and then just collect the rest on the 18th, and that would allow you to get you on Trevor's calendar for this week' — which is the mandated policy from five days earlier. When the prospect explained he had no personal account, the rep took the constraint at face value and stopped. The manager's own taught fallback for this exact situation, taking the card on file and running it on the agreed date, was never offered, and neither was the simpler move of sending the link during the call so it was waiting for him.

objection_plays.detail: 'I have to wait until the closing ... I have to wait until the end, until the 18th' is a timing objection in substance, though a substantially genuine one — he had already said 'The price is not a problem' and named the exact date and mechanism. None of the scripted OD moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the only thing you can control is right now', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. What the rep did instead was better suited to the situation — he verified the constraint was purely logistical and offered a deposit to secure Trevor's calendar. That was the right instinct and it is worth crediting. It scores partial rather than hit because when the deposit was blocked he stopped rather than working the constraint, and because the two moves that cost nothing — sending the payment link during the call, and taking a card to run on the 18th — were never attempted.

Recorded for the rollup as a negative case: no money objection arose on this call at all. The prospect had anchored himself far above the real price — 'I thought it was going to be like 15 or something like that' — and reacted to $6,000 with 'Oh, that's not bad.' No isolation, no open wallet and no financial-picture questions were needed or run. The one probe the rep did make, 'so are you saying that you need the money from this deal to close to do it', was correctly scoped to logistics rather than affordability. This call is the counter-example to the two earlier ones in the batch: where there was no price resistance, no unpublished tier appeared.

Script gap worth escalating. This prospect is sold, solvent and blocked only by the fact that his accountant has just told him to stop running personal spending through his business account, so he has no usable personal account until a deal closes on the 18th. The playbook has no play for a buyer who cannot transact today for a reason that is neither affordability nor hesitation, and P11 assumes payment is collectable on the call. The result was that the strongest-intent prospect in the batch left with nothing collected, nothing sent and nothing booked. A scripted path here — send the link live, take a card dated forward, or provisionally hold the Trevor slot — would have converted this on the call.

notes: Process was strong through discovery and collapsed entirely at the finish. P2 and P3 were run properly and produced the richest material in the batch, and the rep correctly took a 10 out of 10 before naming a price. Two specific coaching points. First, when a prospect hands you 'dad's always been like that, he's always been trying to lose weight, but he doesn't', reflect it straight back as the reframe — that line was the whole call and it was left on the floor. Second, and more expensive: a 10 out of 10 with no price objection must not end with the prospect owning the next action. Send the link on the call, take a forward-dated card, or hold the onboarding slot — all three were available and none were used.
